185 in 40.2 overs in the first ODI, 134 in 41 overs in the second - another excellent bowling display from the Indians. After a rain delay, India had no hesitation in opting to bowl first. Auqib Nabi set the tone upfront with the new ball by removing both the New Zealand openers cheaply. While Arshdeep went wicketless, he gave no freebies with the new ball. Anshul Kamboj, the first-change bowler, struck in his very first over and the hosts were reduced to 23/3. Mitchell and Latham tried to steady the ship but the bowling was disciplined and the batters struggled to get any sort of rhythm going. Mitchell got a reprieve on 21 when he was dropped by Gill of Anshul Kamboj. A couple of overs later, Gurnoor Brar bounced out Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips in the same over, reducing NZ to 53/5. Mitchell and Santner forged a half-century partnership but once that was broken, things unravelled quickly. Mitchell holed out to long-off while trying to loft Axar, Santner fell to Brar in the very next over and New Zealand ended up losing their last 5 wickets for just 22 runs. Brar was the pick of the Indian bowlers on a pace-friendly deck. Yes, the conditions were challenging for batting, but it ain't a 134 wicket as well. India favourties at this point to take a 2-0 lead. Let's see if the New Zealand bowlers can make it interesting..

(On the pitch) Yeah, it's pretty challenging out there. Obviously, we'd always like a few more, but yeah, it's like batting on a trampoline at times. We weren't quite sure what height the ball was going to come through at. We scraped. We tried to do all we could and hopefully something special with the ball and you never know. (One of those surfaces where you feel like you're never really in?) Yeah, look, all of us found it really hard to rotate the strike as well, and especially being, I guess, a drop-in with no pitches either side. It's really hard, I guess, to drop and run and it just stops. So you add that to the bounce, sometimes, yeah, the only best option was to try and give it a hoe and see what happens.

: (On his batting plans) Yeah, I guess just trying to stick to your strengths, and for me, it was when I kind of tried to get a read on what they were trying to do. I was trying to maximise that, but yeah, obviously we wanted to keep extending partnerships as well, and that was probably the challenge, because every time we felt like we got a partnership, we'd lost the wicket. (What did you see out there that you can take to the bowlers? Yeah, look, there's plenty there, first and foremost. Obviously, there's not the run-rate pressure that we would have liked, but yeah, if we can knock off a couple early, get into the middle order, you never know what can happen.

Here's the update.  An anticlimactic end to what promised to be a thrilling finish. " We weren't quite sure what height the ball was going to come through at," was how Daryl Mitchell summed up the pitch during the innings break. He was the only batter to score a half-century and he too was dropped on 21. That tells you how tough it was for the batters. After a delayed start due to rain, India opted to bowl again and bundled out the opponents for 134. Auqib Nabi accounted for the openers and Anshul Kamboj removed Nicholls to reduce NZ to 23/3. Gurnoor bowled a fiery spell - he bounced out Latham and Phillips in the same over, dismissed Santner and then added one more to finish with career-best figures of 4/30. Unlike the previous game, the tail offered no fight.

135 seemed like an easy run-chase but that wasn't the case. Duffy removed the two batters who had looked most comfortable in the previous match. Gill fell for a golden duck, while Kohli managed just 7 after opening his account with a majestic cover drive. Rohit was beaten on multiple occasions. Although he struck four boundaries, he eventually fell to Jamieson. Axar, batting at No. 5 once again, offered catching practice to third man as India slipped to 47/4. Shreyas Iyer and KL Rahul steadied the innings somewhat with a 39-run stand for the fifth wicket before the former was undone by a sharp, in-seaming bouncer from Jamieson. Naman Dhir struck a couple of fours and holed out playing the pull shot. Jamieson picked his 3rd wicket in his final over by dismissing Anshul Kamboj. With 22 runs needed in 21 overs and just three wickets in hand, a new twist came in the form of rain and it failed to relent. India managed to just got over the line as they were ahead by 4 runs on DLS method.

[If he liked bowling here in New Zealand] I really enjoyed it. Bowling here in New Zealand, the bounce and the pace really helped me, so I enjoyed it. [On the bowling plans] obviously, in India the pitches are quite flat, so we have to bowl that hard length. But here, there's that extra bounce. So I was just bowling to my strengths, and it worked. If you're a fast bowler bowling at an average of 140 or 142 (kmph), you have to be aggressive as well. But you have to know your limits too. I just enjoy it and keep bowling. [On using the bouncer] I just try to bowl that hard length, the lengths where batters try to pull. I don't want to bowl it very high; I just keep bowling at shoulder level.

It was a tricky wicket. There's no hiding it. I think they bowled really well, especially at the top, challenged us, and obviously, wickets at the start are never ideal. But I think we were still probably a little bit under at the halfway stage, knowing that there was still a little bit in it, which was nice. And the boys bowled really well. [On the bowling performance] Like we said at Eden Park, it would have been easy for us to just go out there and expect things to happen. But we bowled really well. We started well, and I guess the only way to get into that target was to take wickets at the top. We managed to do that, and then I think the guys coming back in, spell after spell, managed to get the breakthroughs throughout, which is key in ODI cricket.

[On him not bowling today] I warmed up for a little bit, but I think we got up. I think I got pulled, so I just said, "Yeah, you guys look like you're doing all right." It was one of those wickets where the seamers looked pretty challenging on. I know Axar bowled quite nicely, but the Indian quicks were in and around it as well, and they all bowled pretty well. [Lessons from the match] As a batting unit, we know it was going to be a tricky surface. But even if there was a potential way of scraping to 160 or 180, we could have gone from there. But yeah, I think they bowled well as well, and obviously, with the weather around, it's always going to be a bit tough to start, and they exploited it very well. [Update on Tickner] Yeah, he's back at the hotel, so hopefully he pulls up okay. But yeah, he's had a concussion recently, so it's one of those ones you want to give it some time.

: [On the difficult run-chase] As long as we get the win ... it wasn't easy out there. I think we bowled very well. Getting them around 130–140 was good. At one point, we thought it might be an easy target, but we kept losing wickets. We got over the line in the end. [On the bowlers stepping up] Gurnoor, even in the last match as well, has been bowling really well. Hopefully, as he plays more games and gets more experience, he'll become more consistent with his line and length. He's got the pace, he's got the bounce. It's all about how consistent he can be and we saw today the kind of quality he brings if he can keep bowling like this. [Message to the younger bowlers] Most of them have all the qualities that's needed. It's all about performing under pressure. International cricket is all about performing under pressure and getting that experience, bowling day in, day out and trying to deliver under pressure. That's the key point for us. [Areas to improve] Yeah, the pitch was definitely challenging. But I think we lost two extra (wickets) than we would have liked in the end. We knew the rain might come in at the end. And the last two shots that we played ... doesn't look well. If we would have lost this match by DLS, four or five runs, it would have definitely been a stinker for us. But happy to get over the line.

Wellington produced a batting beauty in the T20I contest between the two teams a few days ago, but with rain and moisture around, the bowlers had a field day today. The hosts were skittled out for a mere 134 while the Indians had to sweat to chase the mediocre target. Weather though had the final say and India eked out a 2-0 lead in this 5-match ODI series. We'll now move on to Hamilton for the third ODI on the 10th, with the radar promising more rain. But we'll stay hopeful as we draw curtains on this match. For now, cheers and bye..
